## Headline

**Q3 revenue closed at $38.4M, beating plan by 3.8%**, with gross margin expanding 1.2pts to 76.8% and net income up 38.2%. Burn ticked up 4.1% — within plan and matched by the revenue lift. Runway: 18.4 months at current burn.

## What moved

Revenue tracked above the plan line every week of the quarter, finishing 3.8% above target. The beat was **NRR-driven, not new-logo-driven** — Enterprise subscription expansions delivered $24.8M of the $38.4M, 4.2% above their own plan. New logo bookings landed flat to plan; the lift is the existing customer base growing inside the contract.

**Gross margin lifted 1.2pts to 76.8%** — most of the gain came from the infra optimization that landed in W34. AI infra spend ran 18.4% above plan ($1.58M vs $1.34M), driven entirely by usage growth rather than cost-per-unit increases. **Net income at $4.72M was up 38.2% vs Q2** on the operating leverage between revenue beat and OpEx in-plan.

## So what

We're tracking comfortably ahead of plan on revenue with margin expanding — the rare quarter where both the top line and the unit economics improved. **Runway at 18.4 months gives us optionality** on the Q1 capital plan: we don't NEED to raise, which means we can be selective on terms. The Board update should lead with NRR-driven expansion + margin lift as the durable signals; revenue beat alone is less interesting than the COMPOSITION of the beat.

## Talking points

- **NRR-driven revenue beat is the durable story** — Enterprise subscription expansions delivered $24.8M (vs $23.8M plan). This compounds; new-logo beats don't
- **AI infra over plan by 18.4%** but in a healthy way — usage growth, not cost-per-unit creep. The infra-cost-per-customer metric is flat
- **Sales hiring drove the OpEx delta** — 12 headcount added in Q3 vs 8 planned, deliberately ahead of the up-market motion. Pays back in Q1 quota carry
- **Services revenue light by 1.4%** — only line item below plan; implementation team capacity-constrained. Hiring approved for Q4
- **Runway at 18.4 months** at current burn — gives us optionality on Q1 capital plan. Worth mentioning to the Board even if we have no immediate raise plans

## Risks + caveats

The Q3 revenue beat creates a **tough Q4 comp** — the Polaris Defense expansion and the Helios Manufacturing platform license both landed in Q3 instead of being spread across Q3-Q4 as planned. Without similar Enterprise outliers in Q4, we'd land roughly 4% below the Q3 number, which optically reads as deceleration even though the trend is healthy. Recommend the Board narrative explicitly frame Q3 as exceptional and set Q4 expectations at +1-2% sequential. AI infra growth at 18.4% is the line item to watch — the trend is healthy now but bears monitoring in Q4 when the new model launches.
